messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 502/504 for eu-west-3 private subnets since 2026-03-15T16:12Z. 5xx rate ~18% on api-prod-* routes. Possible egress failures. Suspected recent route-table change. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/eyJ
Morgan (oncall): I’m on it. Logging in to check. can someone confirm any recent infra deploys or route changes? @deploy-bot do you have last apply?
deploy-bot: recent terraform apply by jamal at 2026-03-15T16:09Z — plan included changes to route-table-rtb-0abcde (private subnets) to add a route. No automatic rollback.
Priya (neteng): seeing high connection resets from private instances -> NAT healthchecks failing. quick check: `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=route-table-id,Values=rtb-0abcde --query 'RouteTables[].Routes'` returns:```json
[
  {"DestinationCidrBlock":"0.0.0.0/0","GatewayId":"igw-0ff123","State":"active"},
  {"DestinationCidrBlock":"10.0.0.0/16","NetworkInterfaceId":"eni-0aaa"}
]
```
Priya (neteng): that 0.0.0.0/0 -> igw is the problem for private subnets (traffic should go to nat-0123). looks like the route was accidentally replaced instead of added.
Jamal (infra): ack. I pushed a tf change that updated the shared RTB; I thought it was only for public. My bad. rolling back now.
Morgan (oncall): stop any further changes. Priya you take lead on network fix, Jamal stand by to assist and revert TF. I’ll coordinate customer comms.
Priya (neteng): plan: 1) add explicit route back to nat-0123 with `replace-route` (fast). 2) verify NAT health (elb->nat flow). 3) re-associate correct route table to private subnets if needed. Running replace-route now:```bash
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcde --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0123
```
Priya (neteng): replace-route returned success. now verifying connectivity: running curl from bastion to external service via private instance...
Eli (platform): I’m seeing immediate drop in 5xx on the dashboard for two AZs but one AZ still elevated (az-3). possible NAT in that AZ is unhealthy or missing ENI.
SRE-Emily: can we verify NAT metrics? `aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --nat-gateway-ids nat-0123` shows State: available, but SubnetId: subnet-az3 shows low packets. checking ENIs...
Jamal (infra): I see a stale ENI attachment in az-3 for nat-0123 from 16:05 that failed to initialize during a recent host-scale event. I can try to reattach the ENI or create a replacement NAT in that AZ. what's preferred?
Priya (neteng): temp mitigation: add a route override for subnets in az-3 to point to nat-backup-0456 in az-2 to restore egress. Then we can bring up a replacement NAT or reattach. I'll apply the route for az-3 private RTB:```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-az3-private --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0456
```
Morgan (oncall): go ahead Priya. keep changes minimal and document everything. I’ll start the incident ticket and notify CS.
Kate (customer-success): FYI customers in EU are seeing failed file uploads and webhook retries. I’ve opened a banner for impacted tenants: roughly 6-8% of requests failing, highest for customers pinned to eu-west-3. Please include ETA for mitigation in update.
Priya (neteng): create-route returned success. traffic for az-3 private subnets now routing via nat-0456. Monitoring...
Eli (platform): 5xx down to ~1.2% across region, az-3 now matching baseline. good.
SRE-Emily: follow-up: we need to reconcile TF state and avoid future accidental RTB replacements. Suggest adding a guard to the module to prevent replace-route on shared RTBs. filing a repo PR now.
Jamal (infra): rolling back my TF commit to remove the incorrect route change, creating explicit change to associate only the intended RTB with public subnets. PR opened: https://git.internal/r/infra/changes/5678
Morgan (oncall): summarizing interim mitigation: replaced incorrect route to point back to nat-0123, for az-3 created explicit route to nat-0456 (backup). Customer impact reduced to baseline. Next steps: (1) re-create/repair nat-0123 ENI in az-3 or replace NAT, (2) revert TF drift and add guardrails, (3) post-incident RCA.
Priya (neteng): I can re-create NAT in az-3 now and move routes back after health verified. scheduling low-risk window in 10m.
Kate (customer-success): thanks — please post estimated ETA for full recovery. I’ll update customers: "We rolled out a revert and temporary routing to a backup NAT; service is stable and we expect full restoration within 30 minutes while we finish NAT replacement."
Morgan (oncall): handing to Priya for follow-through. I’m staying on for communications. Priya — you’re primary. :thumbsup:
Priya (neteng): taking over — will post updates.
incident-bot: PAGING UPDATE: incident assigned to Priya (@Priya) at 2026-03-15T16:26Z. Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring.
Priya (neteng): NAT replacement complete in az-3, validated health checks, switched routes back to nat-0123. final verification shows 5xx at 0.3% (within SLO).
Eli (platform): running smoke across affected routes, all green.
SRE-Emily: created short-term repo check: add `prevent_route_replace` boolean to RTB module, added unit tests. PR link: https://git.internal/r/infra/changes/5681
Jamal (infra): confirm TF rollback applied and PR merged to revert accidental change.
Morgan (oncall): closing loop: incident mitigated, customer impact reduced, follow-up RCA to include human error in TF change + module guard. Thanks everyone. :tada:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED by Morgan at 2026-03-15T16:34Z. duration ~22m. root cause: accidental route replacement in shared route table; contributing factor: NAT ENI flakiness in az-3. mitigation: route replace to nat, per-AZ route override to backup NAT, NAT replacement, TF rollback and module guard.
Kate (customer-success): posting post-mortem summary to customers and internal notes. will coordinate with SRE for timeline.
